title: Black Friday Was Named by Angry Cops
sources: History.com (Sarah Pruitt), 'The Real History of Black Friday': in the 1950s Philadelphia police used 'Black Friday' for the chaos the day after Thanksgiving, when suburban shoppers and tourists flooded the city before the Army-Navy game on Saturday; officers could not take the day off and worked extra-long shifts; in 1961 merchants tried to rebrand it 'Big Friday' and failed; the 'in the black' profit explanation spread only in the late 1980s
Britannica, 'Why Is It Called Black Friday?': Philadelphia police origin, 1950s-60s
Philadelphia Inquirer archive / Barry Popik, 'Black Friday (Big Friday)': 1961 Philadelphia 'Big Friday' rebrand attempt

lines.text: Black Friday was named by angry cops.
In the nineteen fifties, in Philadelphia,
the day after Thanksgiving was total chaos.
and football fans poured in for the Army-Navy game.
Police couldn't take the day off,
and worked extra-long shifts in the traffic jams.
So they called it Black Friday.
Stores hated that name, and in nineteen sixty-one, tried Big Friday.
